A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GaussianCity by the same authors. The text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B support reliable comparison across reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original GoogleEarth and KITTI-360 evaluations, a 20-volunteer user study, ablations, and appendix demonstrations of interpolation and relighting.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds density ablations and resource measurements in Table 2.

M1.justification: The BEV-Point initialization, serializer/Transformer decoder, RGB-only prediction, rasterizer, and loss terms match. The added sampling specification and revised loss-weight reporting concern implementation and experimental settings; no new method component or inference procedure is established.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate drone-view generation on GoogleEarth and street-view generation on KITTI-360. Building interpolation and relighting already appear in v1; refreshed examples and density controls do not establish additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain SGAM, PersistentNature, SceneDreamer, InfiniCity, and CityDreamer on GoogleEarth, and StyleGAN2, GSN, GIRAFFE, and UrbanGIRAFFE on KITTI-360. StyleGAN2 remains abbreviated as StyleGAN in Table 1. Region and instance selection were already evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 revises the reported L1/VGG weights from 10 each to initial values of 10 followed by halving every 20,000 epochs. This is a reported setting revision, without establishing reruns. Table 2 adds density-on/off controls and A100 resource comparisons; the standard benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 extends the existing region/instance/ray-intersection analysis with density-removal controls and measurements of memory and runtime in Table 2. Decoder, serialization, and Gaussian-attribute ablations remain, with refreshed qualitative examples. Interpolation and relighting are retained analyses.

E5.justification: Runtime averaging over 100 iterations and the user-study averaging practice are retained. Neither version reports training-seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests.

E6.justification: New Table 2 reports density-off counts of 31M and 38.0K points and resource results, including 1.39 GB and 0.09 seconds for ray intersection with density control. Table 1 and the matched decoder, serialization, and attribute-ablation tables retain their scores. Many qualitative samples are replaced, without establishing a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 newly specifies the style-code distribution as z_i_T ~ N(0,1), whereas v1 only defines the codes as latent vectors. This adds a limited distributional assumption; the remaining mathematical definitions, equations, and geometric assumptions are retained.

C1.justification: Both versions claim efficient unbounded city generation through BEV-Point and its spatially aware decoder, state-of-the-art drone/street-view results, and approximately 60-fold speedup over CityDreamer. The fourth contribution bullet in v2 restates an experimental claim already present in v1.

C2.justification: The explanations concerning spatial structure, instance labels, and RGB-only training stability remain. Both retain the Manhattan/hollow-structure limitations and the relighting shadow caveat. The expanded density discussion repeats the texture-dependent sampling rationale already given in v1 Section 3.2.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents standard-normal style codes, adds the loss-weight decay schedule, and identifies a ray-traversal reference. Optimizers, training budget, batch size, training hardware, and access links remain. The schedule uses epochs while the training budget uses iterations, leaving its intended timing unclear.

R1.justification: v2 adds Amanatides and Woo's voxel-traversal reference and removes the Replica Dataset citation from the scene-generation discussion. The broader positioning remains unchanged; publication-venue updates do not introduce different cited works.

P1.justification: v2 removes the GaussianCity prefix from the title, reformats the contribution list, rewrites the representation-ablation discussion, gives serialization its own paragraph heading, and expands the interpolation explanation. Most prose and the section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one column to two, and Figure 1 moves above the abstract. Numerous qualitative panels are replaced, cropped, or enlarged, and the user-study chart is restyled. Table 2 is added, while v1 Figure 11's two comparison groups become separate Figures 11–12 in v2.

improvement.justification: v1 already provides scaling curves and point counts; v2's Table 2 adds density controls and per-strategy resource measurements, making the central efficiency argument easier to assess. Clearer implementation information and larger visual comparisons provide limited additional value. These gains outweigh small reporting problems: the epochs/iterations ambiguity and the claimed 96% reduction versus instance selection, which Table 2's counts imply is about 95.3%.
